build_spec:
# Calendar Daily Summary — Build Specification (V2.3-6)

## Overview

Build a calendar-only daily summary app. The deliverable is one message per day,
composed from Calendar events (today + tomorrow preview), delivered at a configured
time (default 7 AM).

This is the third gallery app (after Morning Briefing and Note-taker). Unlike
Morning Briefing — which bundles email, weather, and news — this app is
calendar-only. Good for bots whose primary job is schedule awareness.

**Key feature over Morning Briefing:** conflict detection and tight-transition
flagging. If two meetings overlap, or two meetings are within 5 minutes of each
other, the message flags them explicitly.

---

## File Layout

```
scripts/
  calendar_summary.py        ← main CLI: send | preview | status
  calendar-summary-cron.sh   ← cron trigger (calls calendar_summary.py send)
calendar_summary/
  config.json                ← per-bot configuration
  last_run.json              ← last-run metadata (idempotency + status)
```

All paths are relative to the bot's workspace root
(`/Users/{bot_id}/.openclaw/workspace/`).

---

## scripts/calendar_summary.py — CLI

### `send` (runs once daily via LaunchDaemon)

**Steps:**
1. Load config from `calendar_summary/config.json` (fall back to CLI flags).
2. Check idempotency: if `last_run.json` shows today's date + a successful
   send, emit `CAL_SUMMARY_SENT: {date} already-sent` and exit 0 (one per day).
3. Fetch today's events via Calendar skill (Google Calendar API).
4. If `include_tomorrow=true`, fetch tomorrow's events.
5. Detect scheduling conflicts and tight transitions (see Conflict Detection).
6. Compose message (see Message Format).
7. Deliver via `openclaw message send` — reuse the canonical delivery pattern (docs/spec-gallery-delivery-convention-2026-06-11.md; reference implementation in docs/reference/capabilities/template/scripts/example_script.py): resolve (channel, target) from the pod network.json — which lives ONLY at the canonical shared path `/Users/Shared/evolve/network.json` (read it there; it is NOT at `/Users/<bot>/.openclaw/network.json` and NOT in the workspace — copy the `SHARED_DIR = Path('/Users/Shared/evolve')` constant and `load_network()` helper from docs/reference/capabilities/template/scripts/example_script.py verbatim) — reading `bots.<bot_id>.primary_user.external_ids` (channel priority: telegram, whatsapp, signal, imessage, slack, discord, sms, matrix — intersected with the bot's own enabled channels from its openclaw.json `channels.<name>.enabled`, falling back to the best recorded id when there is no overlap so the send fails loudly), then run `openclaw message send --channel=<ch> --target=<target> --message=<text> --json` as the bot user (binary: `shutil.which("openclaw")`, falling back to /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, /usr/bin; cwd = the executing account's pwd-database home, NOT $HOME, so node can resolve its CWD even under sudo-without--H; child PATH prefixed with the CLI's own bin dir so the `#!/usr/bin/env node` entrypoint resolves under launchd's minimal PATH; timeout 60s). Exit code 0 = the channel accepted the send. Never read gateway port/token; never POST to the gateway. If the bot has no recorded delivery route: emit `CAL_SUMMARY_SKIPPED: {date} no-delivery-route` and exit 0 without writing last_run.json.
8. Write `calendar_summary/last_run.json` with today's date, sent_at, counts.
9. Emit `CAL_SUMMARY_SENT: {date} {today_count}ev {conflict_count}conflicts`.

**On Calendar fetch failure:**
- Emit `CAL_SUMMARY_FAILED: {date} calendar-unavailable`.
- Send a short alert: "Calendar summary couldn't run — Calendar access needs
  a refresh. You can fix this from the admin dashboard."
- Exit 1.

### `preview` (dry-run, print to stdout)
Same as send but do not deliver, do not write last_run.json.
Do not check or update idempotency. Useful for testing.

### `status`
Print last-run metadata from `calendar_summary/last_run.json`,
or "No summary sent today yet." if file is absent or stale.

---

## Conflict Detection

Two events CONFLICT when their time ranges overlap:
```
  Event A: [start_a, end_a)
  Event B: [start_b, end_b)
  overlap when: start_a < end_b AND start_b < end_a
```

Two events are a TIGHT TRANSITION when:
- They do NOT overlap (no conflict), AND
- The gap between end of the earlier and start of the later is <= 5 minutes.

Both checks run over today's events only (tomorrow preview is not checked).

Output in the message:
- "Conflicts: none" — when no issues detected.
- "Conflict: 11am sync overlaps with 11:30am client call" — per conflict pair.
- "Tight: 10am standup ends just before 10:05am design review" — per pair.

Implementation note: sort events by start time before checking. Skip events
with missing or unparseable start/end times.

---

## Message Format

### Today with 3 meetings, one conflict:
```
Today — Tuesday, May 13
Today: 3 meetings
• 9:00am — Patel kitchen client (1h)
• 11:00am — Internal sync (30m)
• 11:30am — Robinson site visit (1h)

Conflicts: 11am internal sync overlaps with 11:30am Robinson site visit

Tomorrow: 2 meetings — 10am Wilson estimate review, 3pm vendor call
```

### Today with no meetings:
```
Today — Tuesday, May 13
No meetings today.

Tomorrow: 2 meetings — 10am check-in, 2pm design review
```

### Today with a tight transition:
```
Today — Tuesday, May 13
Today: 2 meetings
• 9:00am — Morning standup (25m)
• 9:25am — Design review (1h)

Conflicts: none
Tight: morning standup ends right before design review (5 min gap)

Tomorrow: nothing scheduled
```

### Without tomorrow preview (include_tomorrow=false):
Omit the Tomorrow: line entirely.

---

## config.json — per-bot configuration

```json
{
  "delivery_time": "{delivery_time}",
  "time_zone": "{time_zone}",
  "include_tomorrow": {include_tomorrow},
  "include_calendar_ids": [],
  "summarize_long_descriptions": false
}
```

Defaults: delivery_time=07:00, time_zone=America/Los_Angeles,
include_tomorrow=true.

The `include_calendar_ids` list (default empty = all calendars) lets the
operator scope the summary to specific calendar IDs (e.g. their work calendar
only, excluding the family calendar).

`summarize_long_descriptions` is a future hook — when true, the forge engine
would call the bot's LLM to compress a long event description to one line.
Default false; LLM use is opt-in.

---

## calendar-summary-cron.sh — cron trigger

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# calendar-summary-cron.sh — calendar summary cron trigger
# Installed by Calendar Daily Summary app. LaunchDaemon fires daily at delivery_time.

WORKSPACE="/Users/{bot_id}/.openclaw/workspace"
LOGFILE="/tmp/{bot_id}-calendar-summary.log"

python3 "$WORKSPACE/scripts/calendar_summary.py" send \
  --time-zone "{time_zone}" \
  >> "$LOGFILE" 2>&1

exit 0
```

Make executable. Register as a LaunchDaemon at {delivery_time} daily.

---

## LaunchDaemon plist

Write to `/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.{bot_id}.calendar-summary.plist`.

System-context LaunchDaemons load at boot regardless of GUI session — required
for headless bots on the mini, where ~/Library/LaunchAgents never load (no
user session). Daemon runs as the bot user via `UserName`.

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN"
  "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
  <key>Label</key>
  <string>com.{bot_id}.calendar-summary</string>
  <key>UserName</key>
  <string>{bot_id}</string>
  <key>GroupName</key>
  <string>staff</string>
  <key>ProgramArguments</key>
  <array>
    <string>/bin/bash</string>
    <string>/Users/{bot_id}/.openclaw/workspace/scripts/calendar-summary-cron.sh</string>
  </array>
  <key>EnvironmentVariables</key>
  <dict>
    <key>TZ</key>
    <string>{time_zone}</string>
  </dict>
  <key>StartCalendarInterval</key>
  <dict>
    <key>Hour</key>
    <integer>{delivery_hour}</integer>
    <key>Minute</key>
    <integer>{delivery_minute}</integer>
  </dict>
  <key>StandardOutPath</key>
  <string>/tmp/{bot_id}-calendar-summary-out.log</string>
  <key>StandardErrorPath</key>
  <string>/tmp/{bot_id}-calendar-summary-err.log</string>
  <key>RunAtLoad</key>
  <false/>
</dict>
</plist>
```

Note: `{delivery_hour}` and `{delivery_minute}` are derived from `{delivery_time}`
("07:00" → Hour=7, Minute=0) by the provisioner at install time.
`{time_zone}` is the IANA timezone string (e.g. "America/Los_Angeles").

---

## Template variables

| Variable | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{bot_id}` | yes | — | Bot user ID (set automatically from install target) |
| `{time_zone}` | no | America/Los_Angeles | IANA timezone for delivery time |
| `{delivery_time}` | no | 07:00 | Delivery time HH:MM (24-hour, local timezone) |
| `{delivery_hour}` | no | 7 | Derived from delivery_time |
| `{delivery_minute}` | no | 0 | Derived from delivery_time |
| `{include_tomorrow}` | no | true | Whether to include tomorrow's preview |

---

## Calendar API access pattern

The Calendar skill (V2.1-3) provides calendar.readonly access via the Google
OpenClaw plugin. The script reads the bot's openclaw.json to find the gateway
port and auth token, then calls the gateway to list events.

Alternatively, the forge engine may wire real Google Calendar API calls via the
bots's installed Google plugin at deploy time. The script must gracefully handle
the case where Calendar access returns an error (emit CAL_SUMMARY_FAILED:).

Stub pattern (for testing — same pattern as briefing.py):
```python
def fetch_calendar_events(time_zone: str, date_str: str) -> tuple[list[dict], str | None]:
    """Return (events, error_note). Events: {id, title, start, end, attendees}."""
    # Stub: production forge engine wires real Calendar access at deploy time.
    return [], None
```

---

## Test sequence

After building:

```bash
# 1. Syntax check
python3 -m py_compile scripts/calendar_summary.py

# 2. Preview (dry-run, no send)
python3 scripts/calendar_summary.py preview --time-zone America/Los_Angeles
# Expected: a formatted calendar summary printed to stdout

# 3. Status (before first send)
python3 scripts/calendar_summary.py status
# Expected: 'No summary sent today yet.'

# 4. Executable check
test -x scripts/calendar-summary-cron.sh && echo 'OK: cron script executable'
```

All steps must exit 0. Step 2 must produce a non-empty message.
